meta.description: Heart-smart recipe conversion rules for reducing sodium, saturated fat, and cholesterol while maintaining flavor
sources: NCBI Bookshelf - Sodium in food preservation
meta.disclaimer: This tool provides general dietary information only. It is NOT medical advice. Always consult your doctor, cardiologist, or registered dietitian before making significant dietary changes, especially if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney disease, or take medications. Individual responses to dietary changes vary.
medical_notes: AHA recommends no more than 2,300 mg sodium/day; ideal limit 1,500 mg/day for most adults
Average American consumes over 3,500 mg sodium daily - more than 150% of recommended
Cutting sodium by 1,000 mg/day can improve blood pressure and heart health
Body needs less than 500 mg sodium/day to function - that's under 1/4 teaspoon salt
Within 2-3 weeks of reducing sodium, taste buds become more sensitive to salt
Saturated fat raises LDL (bad) cholesterol - limit to under 10% of daily calories
Trans fats should be avoided completely - directly increase heart disease risk

dash_diet.label: DASH Diet
dash_diet.description: Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension - clinically proven to lower blood pressure

mediterranean.label: Mediterranean
mediterranean.description: Emphasizes healthy fats (olive oil), fish, fiber

standard.label: Heart-Healthy
standard.description: Based on 4 meals/day within AHA daily limits

strict.label: Low-Sodium Strict
strict.description: For those with existing heart disease or hypertension

original.name: Table salt
original.note: 1 teaspoon salt = 2,300 mg sodium (entire daily limit)

substitutes.name: Half salt + fresh herbs
substitutes.ratio: 1 tsp salt -> 1/2 tsp salt + 1 tbsp fresh herbs
substitutes.prep_notes: Use fresh herbs for maximum flavor impact. Crush dried herbs before adding to release oils.
substitutes.taste_impact: Slightly less salty, more complex herbal flavor

substitutes.name: Salt-free seasoning blend
substitutes.prep_notes: Use more than you would salt. Mrs. Dash, homemade blends, or store brands available.
substitutes.taste_impact: Different but flavorful. May take 2-3 weeks to adjust taste preference.

substitutes.name: Reduced salt + acid (lemon/vinegar)
substitutes.ratio: 1 tsp salt -> 1/4 tsp salt + 1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar
substitutes.prep_notes: Acid brightens flavors similarly to salt. Add near end of cooking.
substitutes.taste_impact: Bright, fresh. Lemon/vinegar adds dimension that compensates for reduced salt.

substitutes.name: Potassium chloride (Nu-Salt, NoSalt)
substitutes.ratio: Use 1/2 to 2/3 the amount of regular salt
substitutes.prep_notes: Has slightly bitter/metallic taste in larger amounts. Works best mixed 50/50 with regular salt.
substitutes.taste_impact: Slightly bitter aftertaste. Less noticeable in cooked dishes.
substitutes.safety_warning: KIDNEY DISEASE WARNING: Potassium chloride can cause dangerous hyperkalemia (high blood potassium) in people with kidney disease or those taking ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or potassium-sparing diuretics. Consult your doctor before using.

original.name: Regular soy sauce
original.note: One tablespoon = 40% of daily sodium limit

substitutes.name: Low-sodium soy sauce
substitutes.prep_notes: Available in most grocery stores. Kikkoman, San-J brands widely available.
substitutes.taste_impact: Very similar to regular soy sauce. Most people cannot tell the difference.
best_for: any recipe calling for soy sauce

substitutes.name: Coconut aminos
substitutes.prep_notes: Made from coconut sap. Naturally sweeter and less salty than soy sauce.
substitutes.taste_impact: Milder, slightly sweeter. Good umami but less intense than soy.

substitutes.name: Liquid aminos (Bragg's)
substitutes.prep_notes: Made from soybeans but not fermented. Gluten-free.
substitutes.taste_impact: Similar to soy sauce, slightly different depth.

original.name: Regular chicken broth
original.note: One cup = 37% of daily sodium limit

substitutes.name: Low-sodium broth
substitutes.prep_notes: Widely available. Swanson, Pacific Foods, store brands.
substitutes.taste_impact: Slightly less rich. Season with herbs and aromatics to boost flavor.

substitutes.name: Homemade unsalted broth
substitutes.prep_notes: Simmer bones/vegetables for 2-4 hours without salt. Add salt only when using in final dish.
substitutes.taste_impact: Control all ingredients. Can be more flavorful than store-bought with proper aromatics.

substitutes.name: No-salt-added bouillon
substitutes.prep_notes: Available from brands like Herb-Ox. Usually in powder or cube form.
substitutes.taste_impact: Less rich than regular bouillon. Add umami boosters like mushrooms or nutritional yeast.

original.name: Regular canned beans
original.note: Canned foods are major sodium sources

substitutes.name: Rinsed canned (1 minute rinse)
substitutes.prep_notes: Rinse canned beans, vegetables under cold water for 1 minute. Reduces sodium by 40%.
substitutes.taste_impact: Minimal difference. Still convenient.

substitutes.name: No-salt-added canned goods
substitutes.prep_notes: Del Monte, Hunt's, store brands offer no-salt versions. Check labels.
substitutes.taste_impact: Slightly less flavorful. Season when cooking.

substitutes.name: Dried beans (cooked from scratch)
substitutes.prep_notes: Soak overnight, cook 1-2 hours. Or use pressure cooker (30-45 minutes). More economical.
substitutes.taste_impact: Better texture, no sodium. Control all seasonings.

processed_meats.label: Bacon, Deli Meats & Processed

original.name: Regular bacon
original.note: Processed meats are very high in sodium

substitutes.name: Reduced-sodium bacon
substitutes.prep_notes: Check labels. Oscar Mayer, Hormel offer reduced-sodium versions.
substitutes.taste_impact: Very similar to regular bacon.

substitutes.name: Turkey bacon
substitutes.prep_notes: Lower in both sodium and saturated fat. Crisps nicely.
substitutes.taste_impact: Slightly different texture. Good smoky flavor.

substitutes.name: Canadian bacon
substitutes.prep_notes: Leaner than regular bacon. Technically ham.
substitutes.taste_impact: Less smoky, more ham-like. Leaner.

substitutes.name: Fresh roasted meat (slice yourself)
substitutes.prep_notes: Roast chicken, turkey, or beef yourself. Slice thin for sandwiches.
substitutes.taste_impact: Fresher, more natural meat flavor. No preservatives.

processed_meats.food_safety_warning: CURING SALT WARNING: Salt (with nitrite) in processed meats prevents botulism. Home-curing without proper salt levels is dangerous. FDA requires minimum 120 ppm sodium nitrite for safety. Do not attempt to reduce salt in home-cured meats without food safety training.

original.name: Parmesan cheese
original.note: Hard aged cheeses tend to be highest in sodium

substitutes.name: Swiss cheese
substitutes.taste_impact: Milder, nuttier flavor. Very low sodium for a cheese.

substitutes.name: Fresh mozzarella
substitutes.taste_impact: Mild, milky, creamy. Much lower sodium than aged cheeses.

substitutes.name: Goat cheese (chevre)
substitutes.taste_impact: Tangy, creamy. Good substitute for feta with less sodium.

substitutes.name: Nutritional yeast
substitutes.ratio: 2 tbsp nutritional yeast per 1 oz Parmesan for cheesy flavor
substitutes.taste_impact: Savory, cheese-like umami. Not identical but adds cheesy depth.

original.name: Butter
original.note: 1 tablespoon butter = ~50% of per-meal saturated fat target

substitutes.name: Olive oil
substitutes.ratio: 3/4 tbsp olive oil per 1 tbsp butter
substitutes.prep_notes: Extra virgin for finishing, regular for cooking. Smoke point 375-405F.
substitutes.taste_impact: Fruity, peppery notes. May change flavor profile in baking.
substitutes.heart_benefit: Monounsaturated fats may improve cholesterol levels

substitutes.name: Avocado oil
substitutes.ratio: 3/4 tbsp avocado oil per 1 tbsp butter
substitutes.prep_notes: High smoke point (520F). Neutral flavor. Good for high-heat cooking.
substitutes.taste_impact: Very neutral. Won't change dish flavor.

substitutes.name: Canola oil
substitutes.ratio: 3/4 tbsp canola oil per 1 tbsp butter
substitutes.prep_notes: Neutral flavor. Contains omega-3s. Good all-purpose oil.
substitutes.taste_impact: Very neutral.

substitutes.name: Unsweetened applesauce (for baking)
substitutes.ratio: 1/2 cup applesauce per 1 cup butter (reduce other liquid slightly)
substitutes.prep_notes: Works best in moist baked goods. May need to reduce sugar slightly.
substitutes.taste_impact: Adds moisture, slight apple sweetness. Denser texture.

substitutes.name: Greek yogurt (for baking)
substitutes.ratio: 1/2 cup Greek yogurt per 1 cup butter
substitutes.prep_notes: Use plain, nonfat or low-fat. Adds protein. Tangy flavor.
substitutes.taste_impact: Tangy, moist. Works well in baked goods.

original.name: Heavy cream
original.note: Heavy cream is very high in saturated fat and cholesterol

substitutes.name: Evaporated skim milk
substitutes.prep_notes: Creamy texture from concentration, not fat. Canned, shelf-stable.
substitutes.taste_impact: Slightly caramelized flavor. Less rich than cream but still creamy.

substitutes.name: Cashew cream
substitutes.prep_notes: Blend 1 cup raw cashews with 1 cup water until smooth. Strain if needed.
substitutes.taste_impact: Neutral, creamy. Mild nutty undertone.

substitutes.name: Silken tofu (blended)
substitutes.prep_notes: Blend until completely smooth. Neutral flavor.
substitutes.taste_impact: Very neutral. Takes on surrounding flavors.

substitutes.name: Plain Greek yogurt
substitutes.prep_notes: Nonfat or low-fat. Nearly identical to sour cream in most uses.
substitutes.taste_impact: Tangier than sour cream. More protein.

original.name: Ground beef 80/20
original.note: Higher fat ground beef is higher in saturated fat

substitutes.name: Lean ground beef 93/7
substitutes.prep_notes: Brown with onions and mushrooms to add moisture. May be drier.
substitutes.taste_impact: Slightly less rich. Still beefy.

substitutes.name: Ground turkey 93/7
substitutes.prep_notes: Season well - turkey is milder than beef. Add Worcestershire sauce for depth.
substitutes.taste_impact: Milder flavor. Takes on seasonings well.

substitutes.name: Ground chicken
substitutes.prep_notes: Very lean - add moisture via onions, breadcrumbs, or grated zucchini.
substitutes.taste_impact: Very mild. Best heavily seasoned.

substitutes.name: Mushroom-beef blend (50/50)
substitutes.ratio: Finely chop mushrooms, mix 1:1 with ground beef
substitutes.prep_notes: Finely dice mushrooms to match beef texture. Saute mushrooms first to remove moisture.
substitutes.taste_impact: Rich, umami. Surprisingly similar to pure beef.

cholesterol_sources.label: High-Cholesterol Ingredients
cholesterol_sources.note: Dietary cholesterol has less impact on blood cholesterol than saturated fat for most people

substitutes.name: Egg whites
substitutes.prep_notes: Lose some richness and binding. For best results, use 1 whole egg + 2 whites per 3 eggs in recipe.
substitutes.taste_impact: Less rich. May affect texture in baking.

substitutes.name: Flax egg (baking)
substitutes.ratio: 1 tbsp ground flax + 3 tbsp water per egg (let sit 5 min)
substitutes.prep_notes: Best for binding in baking. Won't work for scrambled eggs or omelets.
substitutes.taste_impact: Slightly nutty. Works well in hearty baked goods.

substitutes.name: Shrimp (note: low saturated fat)
substitutes.note: Shrimp is high cholesterol but very low in saturated fat. For most people, the saturated fat matters more than dietary cholesterol. 1-2 servings/week is fine for most people.

herbs_fresh.label: Fresh Herbs
herbs_fresh.note: Fresh herbs add more flavor than dried. Use 3x the amount of dried herbs.

italian_seasoning.name: Italian Seasoning
italian_seasoning.homemade_recipe: Mix equal parts dried oregano, basil, thyme, rosemary, marjoram. Store in airtight container.

herbes_de_provence.name: Herbes de Provence
herbes_de_provence.homemade_recipe: 1 tbsp each dried thyme, savory, rosemary, oregano. 2 tsp marjoram. Optional: 1/2 tsp dried lavender.

zaatar.name: Za'atar
zaatar.homemade_recipe: 2 tbsp dried thyme, 1 tbsp each oregano, marjoram, sumac. 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds.

garam_masala.name: Garam Masala
garam_masala.homemade_recipe: 2 tbsp cumin, 2 tbsp coriander, 1 tbsp cardamom, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp each cloves and black pepper. Toast and grind.

cajun_seasoning.name: Cajun Seasoning (salt-free)
cajun_seasoning.homemade_recipe: 2 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp each garlic powder and onion powder, 1 tsp each cayenne, black pepper, thyme, oregano.
cajun_seasoning.note: Commercial Cajun seasoning often contains salt - make your own or check labels

greek_seasoning.name: Greek Seasoning
greek_seasoning.homemade_recipe: 2 tbsp dried oregano, 1 tbsp each garlic powder and onion powder, 1 tsp each dried dill, black pepper. 1/2 tsp each cinnamon and nutmeg.

chinese_five_spice.name: Chinese Five Spice
chinese_five_spice.homemade_recipe: Equal parts ground star anise, cloves, cinnamon, Sichuan peppercorn, fennel seeds.

ras_el_hanout.name: Ras el Hanout
ras_el_hanout.homemade_recipe: 1 tbsp each cumin and coriander. 1 tsp each turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, ginger. 1/2 tsp each cardamom and black pepper.

salt_in_curing.title: Salt Reduction in Cured/Preserved Foods
salt_in_curing.content: Salt plays a critical food safety role in curing meats and preserving foods. A salt concentration of 10% is needed to restrict Clostridium botulinum growth. Sodium nitrite (in combination with salt) is REQUIRED in commercial cured meats to prevent botulism. FDA requires minimum 120 ppm nitrite for safety. Do NOT attempt to reduce salt in home-cured bacon, ham, or other preserved meats without food safety training. This can result in botulism, which is potentially fatal.
safe_alternatives: Buy commercially-made reduced-sodium versions of cured meats
Use fresh meats instead of cured (roast your own turkey for sandwiches)
Reduce portions of cured meats rather than making unsafe home-cured versions

potassium_chloride_warning.title: Potassium Chloride Salt Substitutes
potassium_chloride_warning.content: Salt substitutes containing potassium chloride (Nu-Salt, NoSalt, Morton Salt Substitute) can cause dangerous hyperkalemia (high blood potassium) in susceptible patients. This can cause cardiac arrhythmias and death.
at_risk_groups: People taking ACE inhibitors (lisinopril, enalapril, ramipril)
Older adults with reduced kidney function
potassium_chloride_warning.recommendation: Consult your doctor before using potassium-based salt substitutes. For most people, using herbs, spices, and citrus to reduce sodium is safer.

double_reduction_warning.title: Reducing Salt AND Fat Together
double_reduction_warning.content: When reducing both salt and fat in a recipe, flavor loss compounds. Both salt and fat carry and enhance flavors. Compensate by increasing aromatics (garlic, onion), acids (lemon, vinegar), umami (mushrooms, tomato paste), and fresh herbs significantly. Expect 2-3 weeks for taste buds to adjust.

sodium_reduction: Start by reducing salt 25% - after 2 weeks, reduce another 25%
Taste buds adjust within 2-3 weeks; foods will taste properly seasoned again
Season at the table rather than during cooking - you'll use less
Rinse canned beans and vegetables for 1 minute to reduce sodium 40%
Choose 'no salt added' canned goods, then season yourself
Read labels: items with <140mg sodium per serving are 'low sodium'
Restaurant meals average 1,200mg+ sodium - cook at home for control
saturated_fat_reduction: Choose olive oil or avocado oil instead of butter for most cooking
Use Greek yogurt instead of sour cream (nearly identical in most uses)
Choose leaner cuts: loin, round, sirloin instead of ribeye, chuck
Remove skin from chicken after cooking (keeps meat moist)
Blend mushrooms 50/50 with ground beef for burgers and meatloaf
Use evaporated skim milk instead of heavy cream in soups and sauces
flavor_boosting: Build flavor with aromatics: garlic, onion, shallots sauteed in oil
Add acid (lemon, vinegar) at end of cooking for brightness
Toast spices in dry pan before using to intensify flavor
Use fresh herbs generously - they add flavor without sodium
Add umami: mushrooms, tomato paste, nutritional yeast, parmesan rind
Finish dishes with fresh herbs and a squeeze of citrus
